subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: James Watt and the Steam Engine
description: A short lesson to help you apply James Watt and the Steam Engine.

hook.text: Thomas Newcomen's steam engine wasted 99% of its energy. James Watt thought that was unacceptable.

buildup.text: Newcomen's engine cooled the cylinder every stroke. Watt added a separate condenser to save heat.

discovery.text: Watt's design tripled efficiency. Suddenly steam could power factories, not just pump mines.

twist.text: Watt didn't invent the steam engine. He improved someone else's design — and changed the world.

climax.text: The unit of power — the watt — is named after him. Every lightbulb carries his legacy.

punchline.text: He didn't invent steam power. He made it useful.

quiz.question: What was James Watt's key improvement to the steam engine?
options: He invented a new type of fuel that burned hotter
He added a separate condenser to avoid wasting heat
He made the engine smaller so it fit inside buildings
